IMP-0165.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) UNKNOWN rate computed over the whole candidate set; (2) an invented role name maps to UNKNOWN rather than to its nearest neighbour (no silent snapping).
IMP-0165.question_or_target: Target: extract participant roles and map them onto one normalized vocabulary so 'critic', 'red team' and 'refuter' are comparable. Acceptance: the mapping is a declared table, unmapped roles surface as UNKNOWN (never force-fitted), and the UNKNOWN rate is reported as a number.
IMP-0165.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0165.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: invented role maps to UNKNOWN (both-states: a known synonym maps correctly)
UNKNOWN rate reported as a computed number
IMP-0165.title: Implement role extraction with a normalized role vocabulary

IMP-0194.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) trace replay outcome equality; (2) the cited gap is absent from a fresh gap-finder run (re-measured, not asserted).
IMP-0194.question_or_target: Target: synthesize a workflow from (a) a recorded successful ad-hoc execution trace, or (b) a coverage gap computed by the gap finder. Acceptance: a trace-derived workflow REPLAYS the trace's outcome on the same inputs, and a gap-derived workflow closes the specific gap it cites - each verified by re-running the gap finder afterwards and showing that gap absent.
IMP-0194.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0194.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: trace-derived workflow reproduces the trace outcome
gap-derived workflow removes the cited gap on re-measurement (both-states)
IMP-0194.title: Implement workflow generation from an execution trace or a measured benchmark gap

IMP-0195.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) an unreachable-barrier fixture is rejected while the reachable twin passes; (2) the reachability set is computed by graph traversal and cross-checked against an independent topological sort (two derivations of the same set).
IMP-0195.question_or_target: Target: a static pass over a validated Workflow that reports unreachable nodes, orphan barriers (awaiting something no path produces) and units no node ever schedules. Acceptance: a workflow whose barrier awaits a unit outside every path is REJECTED before dispatch - today validate.py catches barrier-awaits-unknown but not barrier-awaits-unreachable, which is a different defect.
IMP-0195.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0195.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: unreachable barrier rejected; reachable twin accepted (both-states)
traversal-derived and topological-sort-derived reachable sets are equal
IMP-0195.title: Implement static validation: reachability, orphan nodes, unreachable barriers

IMP-0198.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) partition membership is a pure function of the case hash (recomputed independently); (2) a development run that touches a held-out case is detected by an access log assertion.
IMP-0198.question_or_target: Target: build the case corpus workflows are benchmarked on - stratified by difficulty, with a held-out slice never shown during workflow development. Acceptance: the held-out slice is enforced mechanically (a hash-partition, not a convention) so a workflow cannot be tuned on it.
IMP-0198.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0198.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: held-out partition is hash-determined and reproducible
touching a held-out case during development is detected (detector fires)
IMP-0198.title: Construct the matched benchmark case corpus with difficulty stratification

IMP-0202.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a summary-only confirmation is rejected; (2) an artifact-citing confirmation passes and its cited paths are proven to exist by Test-Path before the digest is read.
IMP-0202.question_or_target: Target: before certification, a fresh reviewer that did NOT author the workflow reproduces the benchmark claim from raw sources. Acceptance: the confirmation record must cite the raw artifacts it read; a confirmation that only cites the author's summary is rejected by the gate - a digest is a claim, not a receipt (10646).
IMP-0202.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0202.reviewer_requirement: cross-vendor reviewer (Codex) - independence is the point of the unit
tests_required: summary-only confirmation rejected (both-states)
every cited artifact path is existence-checked before the digest is accepted
IMP-0202.title: Wire the independent-confirmation hook into the certification path

IMP-0204.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) a retired id still resolves and returns the successor; (2) a consumer pinned to the retired id still executes (no hard break) while emitting the warning.
IMP-0204.question_or_target: Target: retire a workflow by SUPERSESSION (naming the replacement and the migration) or DEPRECATION (naming the reason and the removal date), never by deletion. Acceptance: a retired workflow remains resolvable and its consumers get a typed warning with the successor id - silent removal breaks the 'rollback removes existing commands or user data' failure class (11347).
IMP-0204.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0204.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: retired id resolves to successor; pinned consumer still runs (both-states)
deletion attempt on a referenced workflow is refused
IMP-0204.title: Implement deprecation and supersession records for retired workflows

IMP-0218.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) process count returns to baseline after a checkpoint (measured, not assumed); (2) the emitted question carries recommendation + default + durable record, asserted field-by-field.
IMP-0218.question_or_target: Target: on reaching a checkpoint, persist state, emit a terminal envelope with the exact question, and exit - then resume on answer. Acceptance: no process remains resident waiting, measured by process count before and after; and the question presented is ONE foundation-level question with a recommendation and a stated default (the owner-interaction contract at 11364-11370).
IMP-0218.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0218.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: no resident process after checkpoint (process-table measurement)
question payload carries recommendation, tradeoff, default, durable record
IMP-0218.title: Implement the HumanCheckpoint executor as an owner gate that never busy-waits

IMP-0219.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) exit-0-with-missing-receipt expands to zero and reports severed-stream; (2) the healthy twin expands to the expected cardinality.
IMP-0219.question_or_target: Target: expand a dynamic fan-out only after the producer receipt passes the shared completion oracle. Acceptance: a producer that exits 0 with a missing or progress-stream receipt expands to ZERO units and reports severed-stream - exit code zero alone is never success (10646).
IMP-0219.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0219.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: exit-0 + missing receipt => zero expansion + severed-stream (both-states)
progress-stream body is never parsed as a result (assert the taxonomy reason)
IMP-0219.title: Implement the DynamicFanOut executor with an oracle-gated producer receipt

IMP-0221.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) unit accounting after a synthetic storm sums to 100% (completed + typed failures); (2) backoff is bounded - the run terminates rather than retrying indefinitely.
IMP-0221.question_or_target: Question: how should the scheduler behave when a rail starts returning 429? Target: feed measured quota and arrival rate back into admission with bounded backoff. Acceptance: a synthetic 429 storm degrades throughput but produces ZERO lost work units - every unit either completes or carries a typed rate-limited terminal record.
IMP-0221.retry_policy: bounded backoff on rate-limited; two strikes otherwise
IMP-0221.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: synthetic 429 storm: zero lost units (accounting sums to 100%)
backoff bounded; the run reaches a terminal state
IMP-0221.title: Make quota and observed arrival rate first-class scheduler inputs

IMP-0222.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) 49/50 complete with one planted hang (counted); (2) the hung unit's terminal record is timeout-typed, not absent.
IMP-0222.question_or_target: Target: give every work unit its own end-to-end pipeline with its own timeout, so a barrier never waits on a hung sibling beyond that sibling's declared timeout. Acceptance: a deliberately hung unit in a 50-unit cohort delays only itself - the other 49 complete, counted from the ledger. This is a measured orchestration failure on this estate (one hung agent deadlocked a whole phase).
IMP-0222.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0222.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: planted hang: 49/50 complete, 1 typed timeout (both-states with a clean cohort)
no barrier waits past a declared timeout (asserted from timestamps in the ledger)
IMP-0222.title: Implement per-unit pipeline isolation so one hung unit cannot deadlock the cohort

IMP-0224.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) 50 kill-loop iterations leave 50 parseable ledgers (computed pass count); (2) no iteration produces a half-written record (schema check over every line).
IMP-0224.question_or_target: Target: a single append-only run ledger that survives a hard kill mid-write. Acceptance: killing the process during a write leaves the ledger parseable with the partial record ABSENT rather than truncated - verified by a kill-loop test, not by reasoning about atomicity.
IMP-0224.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0224.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: 50/50 kill-loop iterations leave a parseable ledger
zero half-written records across the loop (per-line schema check)
IMP-0224.title: Implement the append-only resumable ledger writer with crash-safe atomic appends

IMP-0228.evidence_requirement: Two signals: (1) cross-machine replay reproduces the plan byte-for-byte (or names the missing input); (2) zero dispatches during replay, counted.
IMP-0228.question_or_target: Target: replay a recorded run, reproducing plan and verdicts with zero dispatch. Acceptance: replay of a run recorded on a DIFFERENT machine still reproduces the plan, proving no hidden host state leaked into the record; if it cannot, the missing input is named rather than the difference being explained away.
IMP-0228.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot - after the second failure on the same error fingerprint, enumerate >=2 alternative approaches before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b); a win-arg-limit failure retries once with --ignore-user-config and a prompt file, never inline argv
IMP-0228.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context
tests_required: cross-machine replay reproduces the plan or names the missing input
zero dispatch during replay (counted, not assumed)
IMP-0228.title: Implement the deterministic replay executor
